rows.description: A friend shouts or grabs and I feel scared and small. Wise action: say "stop, that hurts", step back and fetch a teacher. Hitting back is common at this age but it makes the fight bigger.

rows.description: Another child hands me the toy after a turn. I feel warm and surprised and want to be kind back. Being given a turn teaches that fair sharing feels good, and I learn to offer my own turn later.

rows.description: After the fight I still feel a little cross but I miss playing. Saying "okay, let's play again" or offering a turn is a brave step. Holding a grudge for hours is normal too and needs a gentle nudge, not force.

rows.description: My sibling took the toy I was using and I want to win. I feel both love and fury. A wise child calls a grown-up or agrees on turns; the harmful pattern is pinching, name-calling and telling lies to get the sibling in trouble.

rows.description: The teacher steps in, listens to both of us and sets turns with a timer. I feel safe because someone fair is watching. I learn that big problems can be handed to a trusted adult without being labelled bad.

rows.description: I break my biscuit and give half to a friend who has none. I feel proud and warm inside. Real sharing is chosen, not forced; a wise adult praises the kindness and does not demand I give away everything.

rows.description: My parent says "give it to him right now" before I am ready. I feel angry and confused because it is my favourite thing. Better help is "you may keep it special, but pick another to share". Forced sharing can make a child hold tighter.

rows.description: I see a classmate's shiny box and want it so much my tummy hurts. Envy is normal at this age. Wise action: name the feeling, ask for a turn, or say "I wish I had that". The harmful pattern is hiding it or telling lies about it.

rows.description: I count who got the bigger piece and cry "not fair!" Fairness matters hugely to me. A wise family lets one child cut and the other choose. I learn that equal is not always the same as fair, but that takes years.
